lines: Restitution is not a word. It is what you do next.
Then settle it plainly. Pay, bargain honestly, walk away worse, or make a threat you cannot take back.
If you want this repaired, choose how you mean to repair it.
You caused the harm. Now decide what kind of person you are afterward.
This does not mend itself. Choose your answer carefully.
Payment, a fair bargain, refusal, or threat. Each one says something about you.
The village is listening now. Make your choice with that in mind.
You can still handle this cleanly, but not by standing there silent.
Repair starts with what you do next, not what you wish had happened.
Choose plainly. This moment is already <pulse>heavy</pulse> enough.
Fine. Not free, but less. Pay {payment_count} {payment_items} and this can end cleanly.

Fine. I will take {payment_count} {payment_items}. That is mercy, not forgetfulness.

No. A fair repair does not shrink because it is inconvenient.

Good. Let this be the end of the mistake, not the start of another.

That makes the account even enough to close.
Fine. This matter rests, but the memory stays useful.
You paid what was owed. Now do better with what remains.
That is enough for restitution.
Payment accepted. Let this end <pulse>cleanly</pulse>.

You cannot pay with what you do not have.
